title: Runlight Sherpa coordination — install scrub and tactical log (2026-07-21)
body:
Context:
This is the stitch log from today's Runlight Sherpa coordination scrub. Primary focus: two concurrent installs (Acadia Health on-prem, Citrine Ops VPC) plus a nightshift triage window for the new bootstrap image (linux-5.18+driver bundle). Goal: capture decisions, open blockers, temporary workarounds, and clear next steps for the morning handoff.

Attendees (virtual + boots-on-ground):
- Avery Kim (install lead)
- Diego Ramos (network eng)
- Priya Nair (field SRE)
- Samir Patel (on-call build/packaging)
- Lena Cho (customer success, Acadia contact)
- Marcus (Acadia onsite sysadmin, via phone)

Quick TL;DR:
- Acadia Health install stalled; root cause: intermittent mTLS negotiation failures between Redbox agent and customer KMS proxy when workload nodes had NTP drift > 5s. Temporary mitigation: force ntpd sync + restart redbox-agent.
- Citrine Ops VPC: data-plane perf regression observed after MTU change (9000) on their firewall. Reverted MTU and re-enabled jumbo frames selectively on the compute subnet; latency normalized.
- Bootstrap image 2026.07.20-b2 caused one kernel oops on older NICs; we flagged in CI, rolled back to b1 for nightshift, and opened packaging PR to pin older ixgbe driver for the next build.

Detailed notes:
1) Acadia Health (on-prem)
- Symptom: agent fails to finish config step 3/6; logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts and KMS auth errors (agent -> kms-proxy -> HSM).
- What we tried:
  - Diego: ran tcpdump during handshake; observed SYN/ACKs, then TLS ClientHello retransmits with slightly varying sequence (suggests clock skew or rekey mismatch).
  - Priya: confirmed nodes had 12–17s NTP drift (systemd-timesyncd not hitting pool).
  - Marcus (onsite) forced 'ntpdate pool.ntp.org' and then 'systemctl restart redbox-agent'. Post-restart, agent progressed to step 5 and completed install.
- Root cause hypothesis: customer environment had aggressive iptables rules that delayed/queued UDP NTP responses; drift triggered token timestamps mismatches with the KMS proxy which rejects the challenge.
- Short-term fix (applied): run ntpdate on each node prior to agent start; add preflight check to installer to fail fast if drift > 3s.
- Medium-term actions:
  - Add an installer preflight item (ENG-7201) that checks NTP and warns/auto-sync before agent bootstrap. (Owner: Avery, ETA: 2026-07-28)
  - Document mitigation steps in the field runbook (Owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-07-24)
- Open questions:
  - Should the agent accept a configurable clock-tolerance window? Security team says prefer not to widen tolerance; prefer preflight + explicit instructions.

2) Citrine Ops (VPC)
- Symptom: after customer operator toggled MTU to 9000 in firewall to try to reduce CPU on heavy throughput, we saw 2–3x increase in tail latency for small inference requests and occasional 500 errors from nginx sidecars.
- Investigation:
  - Diego: packet fragmentation and reassembly between firewall and GCE interconnect showed inconsistent MSS handling. Some middleboxes were not advertising expected MSS, causing occasional PMTU blackhole events.
  - Action taken: revert firewall MTU to 1500, enable jumbo on compute-only subnet where switch supports it, and updated route tables to avoid passing jumbo packets through the stateful firewall.
- Result: latency returned to normal within 9 minutes.
- Follow-ups:
  - Create an ops note recommending test plan before MTU change in prod VPCs (Owner: Diego, ETA: 2026-07-26).
  - Add a CI test for small-payload latency under MTU variations in the dedicated test harness (Owner: SRE infra, PR filed).

3) Bootstrap image 2026.07.20-b2 regression
- Symptom: single node kernel oops during driver init on Broadcom NICs in our nightshift lab. Not reproducible on newer hardware.
- Action: pinned last-good driver in b3 candidate and re-ran the full package smoke tests. No more oops.
- PR: ops-private/PR/412 pins ixgbe driver 5.6.x for now. (Owner: Samir, in review)

4) Nightshift triage and operational notes
- Oncall log: 23:10–02:00 — focused on Acadia NTP + Citrine MTU rollback. No customer data exposures.
- Escalations: security was informed of the KMS handshake failures; decision was made to treat as install reliability issue (not a compromise).
- Runbook tweak: add quick checklist for "agent stuck at step 3" with 1) check time sync, 2) tcpdump on 443/8443, 3) KMS proxy health endpoints. (Owner: Priya, ETA: 7/24)

Decisions made during call:
- Do not widen agent clock tolerance. Implement installer preflight and better messaging.
- Revert MTU changes if production latency increases >25% in 5-minute window.
- Rollback policy for bootstrap images: if kernel oops observed in nightlab within 3 hours of deploy, pause rollouts and pin driver version.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Avery: Add NTP preflight check to installer + failure message (ENG-7201) — due 2026-07-28.
- Priya: Draft field runbook section "agent bootstrap blockers" + checklist — due 2026-07-24.
- Diego: MTU test plan and ops note for customers — due 2026-07-26.
- Samir: Finish PR to pin NIC driver and coordinate CI rebuilds — due 2026-07-22.
- Lena: Share Acadia post-install notes with Customer Success for a short howto (ntp steps we ran) — due 2026-07-23.

Notes to self / messy fragments (keep here until captured in runbook):
- Consider adding an installer flag --force-ntp-sync that will run ntpdate as a last resort (danger: modifies sysadmin config) — bring up with security and field leads.
- We should log an automatic 'time-drift' metric for installs and ship that to Console for correlation with failed bootstraps. Low-effort: metric emitted by agent before TLS handshake.
- Could we make redbox-agent do a health-check loop for KMS handshake and surface better errors? Right now errors are generic TLS timeout.

Post-mortem plan if similar incident occurs (short runbook):
1) Check agent logs; grep for "KMS auth" and "handshake timeout".
2) Run ntpdate; if drift > 5s, hold install.
3) If restart fixes — collect tcpdump + redbox-agent logs and mark incident for follow-up.
4) If restart does not fix — escalate to infra-net and security.

Parking lot / longer-term ideas:
- Autonomous preflight that negotiates with customer's firewall to detect PMTU / MSS mismatches before we start heavy traffic.
- A small "install diagnostics" container we can run that exercises TLS+KMS flows with verbose output for customers to run locally with support.

Appendix: useful commands observed during troubleshooting (copyable)
- sudo ntpdate -b pool.ntp.org && systemctl restart redbox-agent
- sudo tcpdump -nni any port 443 or port 8443 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap
- journalctl -u redbox-agent -f --since "10 minutes ago"
- ip route show; ip link show; sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward

Meeting rating: productive but noisy; need better preflight checks rather than relying on nightshift fixes.

Next sync: daily 09:30 PDT runlight sherpa standup (short) — tomorrow 2026-07-22.
